questions.question: 按托利对「钟表时间」和「心理时间」的区分，下面哪一种是他主张放下的？
options: 定一个五年职业目标，并且每个季度认真检查一次自己的进展
觉得「等我升职了就好了」，把满足推到将来
回顾上一个失败的项目，把教训整理成一份清单
为下周的会议提前排好日程，并准备好要讲的材料
questions.explanation: 托利保留钟表时间：计划、约定、从过去学经验都要用。他反对的是心理时间——拿过去当身份、拿未来当救赎，为了别的时刻否定这一刻。定长期目标也属于钟表时间，问题只在把平静挂在目标上。
questions.question_en: Under Tolle's distinction between clock time and psychological time, which of these is he asking you to let go of?
options_en: Setting a five-year career goal and carefully checking your progress every quarter
Feeling that life will be fine once you get promoted, deferring contentment to the future
Reviewing a failed project and writing up a list of lessons learned
Scheduling next week's meeting in advance and preparing what you'll present
questions.explanation_en: Tolle keeps clock time: planning, appointments and learning from the past all stay. What he opposes is psychological time — using the past as identity and the future as salvation, denying this moment for another. Long-term goals belong to clock time too; the trouble is only in hanging your peace on them.

questions.question: 托利谈「臣服」时说，身处难以忍受的处境，痛苦的主要来源是什么？
options: 急于行动，没有先花足够时间把处境想清楚
过早地在心里接受了处境，于是放弃了本可以去改变它的那些努力
处境本身恶劣到超出了一个人能承受的限度
不走、不改、又不接受，只在心里抱怨和抵抗
questions.explanation: 托利给出三个选项：离开、改变、或完全接受；最苦的是第四种，不走不改又不接受。臣服不是认命，是不再在内心抗拒「此刻已经是这样」，然后照样可以行动——陷在泥里先承认，再全力想办法出来。
questions.question_en: Discussing surrender, what does Tolle say is the main source of suffering when a situation feels intolerable?
options_en: Rushing to act before taking enough time to think the situation through
Accepting the situation inwardly too early, and so giving up efforts that could have changed it
The situation itself being worse than a person can bear
Neither leaving, changing it, nor accepting it — just complaining and resisting inwardly
questions.explanation_en: Tolle offers three options: leave, change it, or accept it fully. The worst is a fourth — staying, not changing, and not accepting. Surrender isn't resignation; it's ceasing inner resistance to what already is, and you can still act — admit you're stuck in the mud, then put everything into getting out.

questions.question: 当一股异常沉重的情绪（托利所说的「痛苦之身」）升起时，他建议怎么做？
options: 先把情绪压住、不让它表现出来，以免说出伤人的话
把感受原原本本地说给对方听，让情绪宣泄出去
认出它，在身体里完整地感受，不顺着念头编故事
有意识地用积极的念头替换掉负面念头，一直坚持到情绪慢慢平复下来
questions.explanation: 托利的方法是「看着它」：痛苦之身靠你和它认同来存活，你成为观察者，它就喂不到念头。他特别强调这不是压抑——压抑本身是抗拒，会喂养痛苦之身；要的是完整地感受，只是不行动、不讲故事。
questions.question_en: When an unusually heavy surge of emotion arises — what Tolle calls the pain-body — what does he advise?
options_en: Hold the feeling down and keep it from showing so you don't say something hurtful
Tell the other person exactly how you feel so the emotion gets vented
Recognize it and feel it fully in the body, without following its thoughts into a story
Deliberately replacing negative thoughts with positive ones and keeping at it until the feeling subsides
questions.explanation_en: Tolle's method is to watch it: the pain-body survives on your identification with it, and once you become the observer it can't feed on your thinking. He stresses this is not suppression — suppression is resistance and feeds the pain-body; the point is to feel it completely without acting it out or narrating it.
